name: The Good Food Institute
beneficiaries_note: Our build: the alternative-protein market GFI works on is global, and so is the good at the defaults (the tonnes and their ammonia, spread over the world by population; eaters' health and the animals spared wherever the meat would have been eaten): a judgment, as no country split of the market's future gain exists.
summary: The Good Food Institute, a US non-profit with six affiliates abroad, funds open-access research, works for public funding and fair rules, and helps companies and investors, so that plant-based, cultivated and fermentation-made foods replace more meat, seafood, milk and eggs; this model covers all of its 2024 programmes ($26.5m) as one chain: the market gain the whole field's resources bring forward, credited to GFI by its share of those resources. At the site's defaults it comes to about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, nearly two thirds from the greenhouse gases and farm ammonia of the animal products displaced, about a third from eaters' health (a side effect) and under one percent from the animals spared. The biggest uncertainty is how much of the meat market alternative proteins will take (our judgment, half a point to 15 points), then how far a GFI dollar goes against the field's average dollar; nothing here is measured, so the whole result is discounted for missing outcome data.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for every animal model. The shared SAD figures are Ambitious Impact's, which count each species' pain as a share of a person's with its own species weights. Here those weights come out and Rethink Priorities' go in, so every species is counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain. How a chicken compares with a person is the one animal slider.

rows.label: Meat in one meat meal (kg, carcass weight)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, to count meat as meals: a portion of about 100 g of retail meat is about 0.15 kg in carcass weight (retail cuts are roughly 60-75% of the carcass). Range 0.1 kg (smaller portions, mixed dishes) to 0.25 kg (US-sized portions).

rows.label: Meat meals a year worldwide
Kilograms per tonne
Share of the world's meat market alternative proteins gain once the field's work pays off
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the main uncertainty: how much more of the world's meat demand plant-based, cultivated and fermentation-made products take, beyond today's share, once the research, public funding and company work now under way have borne fruit (about 15 years, below). Today: global retail sales of plant-based meat and seafood were $6.1 billion in 2024 (Euromonitor, via GFI, reported by Food Business Middle East & Africa, foodbusinessmea.com, 2025), against a meat market of over a trillion dollars, about half of one percent; US plant-based food sales fell 4% in dollars and 5% in units from 2023 (SPINS, via GFI's 2024 State of Alternative Proteins, p. 7), so growth has stalled, and the average product does not yet match meat on taste and price (GFI's own 2024 report). Industry forecasts of a tenth of the protein market by 2035 (Boston Consulting Group and Blue Horizon, 2021) were made before the stall. Best guess 3 points of the meat market, range half a point (the field stays a niche) to 15 points (taste and price parity reached for the main products).

rows.label: Dairy meals replaced, per meat or seafood meal replaced
rows.explainer: Our judgment: plant-based and fermentation-made milk, cheese and yoghurt are a large part of the field (plant-based milk is the biggest plant-based category; fermentation companies, which raised the most in 2024, make mostly dairy and egg proteins), and their resources are in GFI's credit below, so their gain counts too. Plant-based milk already has a far larger share of its market than plant-based meat has of meat (US household penetration about 40% against 13%, GFI). Best guess 0.4 dairy servings per meat or seafood meal replaced, range 0.15 to 0.8.

rows.label: Egg meals replaced, per meat or seafood meal replaced
rows.explainer: Our judgment: plant-based and fermentation-made eggs are a small but growing category (US plant-based egg sales up 11% from 2021 to 2023 and 2% in 2024, GFI's 2024 State of Alternative Proteins p. 9). 0.1 egg meals per meat or seafood meal replaced, range 0.03 to 0.3.

rows.label: Meat and seafood meals a year replaced once the field's work pays off
rows.explainer: The meat meals the gain replaces, plus the seafood meals replaced alongside them in the analogues' shared mix (seafood_share of all meat and seafood analogue meals).

rows.label: Animal-product meals a year replaced once the field's work pays off

rows.label: The place's meal against the reference meal
rows.explainer: 1, range 0.5-2: the market is global, and the site's meal-mix rule (docs/normalization.md 2.9) puts global meals at 1 (US meals 1.5; the US is about a third of the market). The product mix alternative proteins replace is the step above.

rows.label: SADs averted per egg meal replaced

rows.label: SADs averted per dairy meal replaced

rows.label: Share of meat and seafood analogues that replace seafood
rows.explainer: The shared figure ({{row:seafood_share}}, 1-10%) behind the product-mix ratio, used here to add the seafood meals replaced alongside the meat meals and to weight seafood's meal size, emissions and health effect.

rows.label: Fall in production per meal not eaten
rows.explainer: Fewer meals bought lowers production by less than one for one, because prices fall and others buy more (Norwood and Lusk 2011). Emissions follow production, so the tonnes below take it too.

rows.label: Years the field's progress is brought forward
rows.explainer: The site's one number of years a won change counts before it would have come anyway (docs/normalization.md 2.9). Here the change is the alternative-protein market reaching the share above; all the resources the field puts in until then (below) bring it forward by these years, and GFI is credited with its share of those resources.

rows.label: Years until the gain is reached
rows.explainer: The site's shared wait for technologies not yet deployed (15 years, 8-25): research and scale-up now, products at parity and market share later.

rows.label: Discount for the wait
Discounted years of impact
Greenhouse gases avoided per kg of meat displaced, net of the alternative (kg CO2e per kg carcass)
rows.explainer: Our judgment from Poore and Nemecek (2018), global means per kg of retail product (Our World in Data's copy): beef herd 99.5 kg CO2e, dairy herd beef 33.3, lamb 39.7, pig meat 12.3, poultry 9.9, tofu 3.2. Weighted by FAO's 2024 production (pig 125 Mt, poultry 150 Mt, bovine 78 Mt half each herd, sheep and goat 19 Mt) that is 24 per kg of retail meat, about 17 per kg of carcass (retail about 0.7 of carcass), less about 2 for the alternative (tofu as a stand-in): about 15. Range 7 (alternatives displace mostly chicken and pork) to 30 (mostly beef).

rows.label: Greenhouse gases avoided per kg of fish displaced, net of the alternative (kg CO2e per kg live weight)
rows.explainer: Our judgment: Poore and Nemecek's farmed fish is 13.6 kg CO2e per kg of product (Our World in Data's copy), about 6-7 per kg live weight; wild capture, about half of aquatic animal production (FAO: aquaculture 51%), emits mainly fishing boats' fuel, about 2 per kg landed (Parker et al. 2018, Nature Climate Change). Average about 4.3, less a little for the alternative: 4. Range 2 (wild fish) to 8 (farmed shrimp and salmon).

rows.label: Greenhouse gases avoided per dairy meal replaced, net (kg CO2e)
rows.explainer: Our judgment from Poore and Nemecek (2018, Our World in Data's copy): milk 3.15 kg CO2e per kg against soy milk 0.98, so a 250 ml serving saves about 0.55. Range 0.2 (milk in tea and coffee) to 1.5 (cheese, about ten litres of milk per kg).

rows.label: Greenhouse gases avoided per egg meal replaced, net (kg CO2e)
rows.explainer: Our judgment from Poore and Nemecek (2018, Our World in Data's copy): eggs 4.67 kg CO2e per kg, so two eggs (0.12 kg) emit about 0.56, less about 0.1 for a plant-based alternative. Range 0.2 to 0.8.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO2e avoided per meat or seafood meal replaced
rows.formula: ((1 - seafood_share) * meat_per_meal_kg * net_kg_co2e_per_kg_meat + seafood_share * seafood_per_meal_kg * seafood_net_kg_co2e_per_kg) / kg_per_tonne

rows.label: Tonnes of CO2e avoided by the dairy and egg meals replaced with each meat or seafood meal
Healthy years gained by eaters per kg of meat displaced
rows.explainer: A side effect on the eaters' health (land meat only), our judgment. GBD 2021 attributes 2.41 million DALYs a year to diets high in red meat through breast cancer alone (PMC12107595), and more through colorectal cancer, diabetes and heart disease; over about 220 million tonnes of red meat that is at least 0.00001 per kg for breast cancer alone. But poultry, a large part of what is displaced, carries no such risk, the evidence for unprocessed red meat is weak (Burden of Proof, Lescinsky et al. 2022, one star), and the alternatives are processed foods with salt and fat of their own. Best guess 0.00001 per kg of carcass, range -0.000005 (a small net harm) to 0.00006 (the larger GBD burden in full).

rows.label: Healthy years gained by eaters per kg of fish displaced (live weight)
rows.explainer: A side effect on eaters' health, our judgment: replacing fish loses its omega-3 fatty acids (GBD counts a diet low in seafood omega-3 as a risk) unless the alternative is fortified, and fish carries no cancer risk like red meat's. A small loss, -0.000005 per kg live weight, range -0.00002 to a small gain (0.000002, fortified alternatives and less mercury).

rows.label: Healthy years gained by eaters per meat or seafood meal replaced
rows.formula: (1 - seafood_share) * meat_per_meal_kg * health_dalys_per_kg_meat + seafood_share * seafood_per_meal_kg * seafood_health_dalys_per_kg
rows.explainer: Land meat's and seafood's effects by the analogues' mix; dairy and egg meals carry none here.

rows.label: All resources the field puts in until the gain is reached (US$)
rows.explainer: Everything spent so far plus today's yearly resources for the years until the gain (no growth or decline assumed; 2024's investment was well below 2021's). This is the denominator of GFI's credit, as for research credited by its share of the field's spending until results arrive (docs/normalization.md 2.9). Past spending is in it although today's small market is not in the gain: it built the companies, research and rules the future gain rests on, so the future gain is the result of all of it. Today's share is not in the gain, although the money that bought it is in the denominator, because the same money also built the base for the future gain.

rows.label: GFI's share of all the resources behind the gain
rows.explainer: One year of GFI's spending over everything the field spends until the gain (Convention 2: credit by share of resources). Under 0.1%: GFI is a small part of the money, and its dollar's particular reach is the leverage row below, not a bigger share.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Share of credit used
Meat not eaten per meal of alternative protein eaten
rows.explainer: Our judgment: not every alternative-protein meal displaces a meat meal; some replace beans, other vegetarian food or nothing (added variety). Studies of US retail data find plant-based meat purchases substitute only partly for beef and other meat. Best guess half, range 0.2-0.8.

rows.label: A GFI dollar against an average dollar into the field
rows.explainer: Our judgment. GFI's money buys things the field's average (venture) dollar doesn't: open-access research and research grants anyone can use ($3.7m of grants in 2024), work on public funding and rules (product bans and labelling laws largely overturned in the US, Brazil and Asia Pacific, GFI's 2024 State of Alternative Proteins, p. 29), and talent and information for the whole field. Anchor: open, publicly funded research draws in private research money. Moretti, Steinwender and Van Reenen (2025, Review of Economics and Statistics) find that a 10% rise in government-funded R&D raises privately funded R&D by about 5-6%, an elasticity of about 0.5. With the field's private investment ($1.1bn in 2024) about 1.5 times its public and open research money, each open-research dollar draws in about 0.5 × 1.5 = 0.75 private dollars, so it is worth about 1.75 average dollars. About 60% of GFI's programme money is science and policy (Science and Technology and Policy, $16.1m of $26.5m); counting the rest (communication, convening, corporate advice) at about 0.7 of an average dollar gives 0.6 × 1.75 + 0.4 × 0.7 = 1.3. Range 0.5 (little of it draws in anyone) to 5 (its policy work moves public money several times its cost).

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no measurement links GFI's work to meals displaced; the chain is the market's outlook and judged credit. The shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: Read by the tonnes' bridge, as by the tco2e unit's conversion. Livestock burn little fuel, but manure and fertiliser for feed release ammonia, which forms fine particles: Domingo et al. (2021, PNAS) find 15,900 US deaths a year from the air pollution of food production, 80% from animal-based foods, about 12,700. Over the roughly 400 million tonnes of CO2e a year of US animal agriculture (EPA's Inventory of US Greenhouse Gas Emissions 1990-2022: enteric fermentation 192.6 million tonnes in 2022, manure management about 82, and our judged share, about 40%, of agricultural soil management's nitrous oxide for feed crops, about 120, out of the sector's 593.4) that is about 0.3 deaths per 10,000 tonnes, about 0.2 of the fossil-fuel average's 1.46. Range 0.05 to 0.45 (places with more or fewer people near farms; Lelieveld et al. 2015 put agriculture at a fifth of outdoor air-pollution deaths worldwide).

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (none here)
rows.explainer: 0: the ammonia's deaths are in air_pollution_weight, so nothing is counted twice.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes that are methane
rows.explainer: Our judgment: FAO's 2013 assessment of livestock emissions (Tackling Climate Change Through Livestock) put methane at about 44% of the sector's emissions, with nitrous oxide and carbon dioxide the rest; its 2023 GLEAM update puts enteric and manure emissions (methane and nitrous oxide) at about 60%. Weighted by tonnes, beef's enteric methane dominates. Range 0.3 (alternatives displace mostly chicken and pork, whose emissions are mostly feed and energy) to 0.55.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO2e avoided per dollar you give
Tonnes avoided, in chicken-equivalent pain days per dollar you give
rows.formula: tco2e_bridged * (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier) / ($chicken_vs_person * $daly_per_sad * $uov_per_daly)
rows.explainer: The bridge from tonnes into this model's unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): the headline multiplies the unit's conversion back, so the tonnes reach healthy years through the climate unit's own conversion and move with the climate sliders, not the animal one.
